School of Electrical and Mechanical Engineering
Show menu
Advancing electrical and mechanical engineering, and aviation knowledge for global impact
Adelaide University’s Electrical, Mechanical, Maritime and Aviation programs combine theory, hands-on experience, and industry engagement. Students gain expertise in their chosen fields, such as robotics, control systems, energy systems, electronics, telecommunications, aviation operations, and safety.
With world-class facilities and industry partnerships, graduates are career-ready, prepared to innovate, lead, and make meaningful contributions across engineering and aviation sectors globally.
Study areas
Aviation
Embark on an exhilarating journey in aviation with a degree from Adelaide University. Be part of an industry that underpins the global economy, facilitating the transport of goods and connecting people worldwide.

Biomedical Engineering
Biomedical Engineering integrates expertise across biophotonics, biomedical instrumentation and sensors, biomechanics, medical imaging, and signal processing. We focus on applications in neural engineering, wearable technologies, and medical devices, spanning modelling, integrated circuits, prototyping, and preclinical trials, while leveraging medical machine learning to deliver transformative healthcare solutions.
If you’re passionate about becoming a biomedical engineer and driving innovative healthcare solutions, an electrical or mechanical engineering bachelor’s degree at Adelaide University with specialisation in Biomedical Engineering is the ideal place to start.

Electrical Engineering
Within the Electrical and Electronic Engineering discipline, we are experts in applied physical sciences, technology, energy, and information systems. We are committed to solving real-world problems through fundamental and applied research.
If you’re looking to become an electrical engineer and excited about solving real-world problems, an engineering degree at Adelaide University is for you.

Engineering Management
Engineering Management focuses on how complex engineering projects and systems are planned, optimised, and delivered. It brings together technical expertise with strategic leadership that drives high‑performing organisations. The degree builds expertise in engineering economic analysis, total quality management, enterprise resource planning, operations and supply chain management, circular economy principles, sustainable engineering, and data‑driven decision‑making.

Mechanical Engineering
Our Mechanical Engineering discipline focuses on how the physical world moves. It covers expertise in aerospace, acoustic and vibration, control and dynamics, robotics and automation, design and systems, energy science and engineering, fluids and heat transfer, nanoscale materials and mechanics of materials, biomechanical engineering, maritime and naval engineering, aerospace and aeronautical engineering, and advanced manufacturing.
If you’re looking to become a mechanical engineer and innovating how things move, an engineering degree at Adelaide University is for you.
